newsitem.title: MEXICO: Top Mexican officials to run in election -report.
newsitem.headline: Top Mexican officials to run in election -report.

text.p: Several Mexican cabinet members will resign in the coming weeks to run for the Senate in July's mid-term elections, a Mexican newspaper reported on Thursday.

El Universal newspaper said Foreign Minister Jose Angel Gurria, Commerce Secretary Herminio Blanco, Energy Secretary Jesus Reyes Heroles and Social Development Secretary Carlos Rojas all plan to run for Senate seats up for grabs on July 6.
Officials at the PRI were unavailable for comment on the report. Thursday and Friday are national holidays in Mexico.

Recent rule changes by the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) require that the party's presidential candidate must have held a previous elected post, something most Mexican cabinet members have not done.

Although the Senate holds little real power in Mexico, many top politicians are expected to join congressional and state races in order to be included in the party's list of potential candidates for national elections in 2000, a list known here as the "presidenciables".

The newspaper, which did not reveal its sources for the article, said the men are part of a larger list of candidates that the PRI, which has ruled here for 68 consecutive years, will unveil in early April.
